ai.literal: Unfailing harvest-and, worthy people-and, decline-without wealthy people-and, coming together is a country.
ai.translation: A country is that which brings together unfailing harvests, worthy people, and wealthy citizens free from decline.
ai.modern: குறையாத விளைச்சலும், தகுதியுடைய சான்றோர்களும், வறுமையோ தாழ்வோ இல்லாத செல்வந்தர்களும் ஒன்று கூடி வாழ்வதே ஒரு சிறந்த நாடாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the three essential components that constitute a great nation. First, it must have 'taḷḷā viḷaiyuḷ', which refers to agricultural yields that never fail, ensuring food security. Second, it must have 'takkār', meaning righteous and worthy people who maintain moral order. Third, it must have 'tāḻvilā celvar', wealthy citizens whose prosperity does not decline, enabling them to support others and contribute to the state's economy.

ai.literal: By great wealth becoming that which is desired, and by rare ruin, yielding abundantly, is a country.
ai.translation: A true country is one that is coveted by others for its immense wealth, yet remains free from devastating ruin, yielding food and resources in great abundance.
ai.modern: மிகுந்த செல்வத்தால் பிற நாடுகள் விரும்பத்தக்கதாகி, எவ்வித அழிவும் இல்லாமல், மிக அதிகமாக விளைச்சலைத் தருவதே சிறந்த நாடாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the essential economic and physical qualities of a prosperous nation. First, it must possess great wealth so that it is highly valued and desired by others. Second, it must be free from devastating calamities, pests, or external destruction, ensuring safety. Finally, it must naturally yield agricultural and material produce in great abundance. Together, these elements of wealth, security, and high productivity constitute a true country.

ai.literal: Bearing completely the burden when it comes upon it, and paying completely the tax to the ruler, is a country.
ai.translation: A true country is one that bears the entire burden when extra weight comes upon it, and pays its taxes fully to the ruler.
ai.modern: கூடுதல் சுமை தன்மேல் வரும்போது அதை முழுமையாகத் தாங்கிக்கொண்டு, அரசனுக்குச் செலுத்த வேண்டிய வரிகளையும் முழுமையாகச் செலுத்துவதே சிறந்த நாடாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the economic and social resilience of a great nation. A true country must have the capacity to bear sudden, heavy burdens—such as supporting refugees or surviving natural disasters—without collapsing. At the same time, its citizens must remain prosperous enough to pay their taxes and dues fully to the sovereign. The word 'poṟai' refers to the external or unexpected burdens, while 'iṟai' refers to the regular taxes paid to the ruler.

ai.literal: Intense hunger and unceasing disease and destructive enmity not entering, that which functions is a country.
ai.translation: A true country is that which functions without ever being afflicted by intense hunger, unceasing disease, and destructive enmity.
ai.modern: மிக்க பசியும், நீங்காத நோயும், அழிவு செய்யும் பகையும் வந்து சேராமல் நடைபெறுவதே நாடாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the essential qualities of a prosperous and peaceful nation. A true country must be free from three major scourges: extreme hunger (famine), persistent epidemics or diseases, and destructive external or internal enemies. The word 'உறுபசி' refers to intense, widespread hunger, while 'ஓவாப் பிணி' denotes diseases that never seem to leave the population. 'செறுபகை' represents hostile forces that seek to destroy. Only when a land is naturally free from these three afflictions can it function successfully as a true nation.

ai.literal: Many factions, ruin-causing internal enmity, and ruler-harassing destructive rebellious chieftains, that which is without is a country.
ai.translation: A true country is one that is free from warring factions, ruinous internal enmities, and murderous, rebellious chieftains who harass the ruler.
ai.modern: பல பிரிவுகளாகப் பிரிந்து சண்டையிடும் குழுக்களும், நாட்டைப் பாழாக்கும் உட்பகையும், அரசனைத் துன்புறுத்தும் கொலைத்தொழில் புரியும் குறும்நில மன்னர்களும் இல்லாததே சிறந்த நாடாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines a stable nation by identifying three internal threats it must be free from. First, 'palkuḻu' refers to multiple conflicting factions or sects that divide the populace. Second, 'uṭpakai' represents treasonous internal enmity that quietly ruins the state from within. Third, 'koṟumpu' refers to rebellious, lawless chieftains or marauders who harass the sovereign ruler and disrupt governance. A prosperous and secure country is one that remains entirely free from these three destructive forces.

ai.literal: Ruin not-knowing, even in ruined condition prosperity undiminishing country, they say, of countries the foremost.
ai.translation: A country that knows no ruin, and whose prosperity does not diminish even if it suffers a setback, is said to be the foremost among nations.
ai.modern: அழிவை அறியாததும், ஒருவேளை அழிவு வந்த காலத்திலும் தன் வளம் குறையாததுமான நாடே நாடுகளுள் தலைசிறந்தது என்று கூறுவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the supreme qualities of an ideal nation. The key phrase 'கேடறியா' (knowing no ruin) highlights a land so secure and well-governed that it is free from external invasions and internal disasters. Even if some misfortune or temporary setback ('கெட்ட இடத்தும்') does occur, its inherent strength ensures that its prosperity ('வளம்') remains undiminished ('குன்றா'). Such a resilient and self-sustaining land is declared by wise people to be the crown or foremost ('தலை') among all countries.

ai.literal: The two waters, and a well-situated mountain, and flowing water, and a strong fortress, are the essential parts for a country.
ai.translation: The two sources of water, a well-situated mountain, flowing river water, and a strong fortress are the essential constituents of a country.
ai.modern: மேல்நிலை நீர், கீழ்நிலை நீர் ஆகிய இருவகை நீர்வளமும், தக்க இடத்தில் அமைந்த மலையும், ஓடிவரும் ஆற்று நீரும், வலிமையான அரணும் ஒரு நாட்டிற்கு இன்றியமையாத உறுப்புகளாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet lists the five essential physical features that constitute a prosperous and secure nation. The term 'இருபுனல்' refers to the two primary sources of water: rain (or surface water) and underground spring or well water. A 'வாய்ந்த மலை' is a mountain situated in a way that offers natural resources and protection. 'வருபுனல்' refers to flowing water, such as rivers that continuously feed the agricultural lands. Finally, 'வல்லரண்' is a strong, impenetrable fortress for defense. Together, these water sources, natural barriers, and defenses form the vital limbs of a country.

ai.literal: Absence of disease, wealth, abundant yield, happiness, protection—these five, they say, are the ornaments of a country.
ai.translation: Freedom from disease, wealth, abundant harvest, happiness, and strong security—these five, they say, are the jewels of a country.
ai.modern: நோயற்ற வாழ்வு, செல்வம், நல்ல விளைச்சல், இன்பம், பாதுகாப்பு ஆகிய இந்த ஐந்தும் ஒரு நாட்டின் அணிகலன்கள் என்று கூறுவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the five essential elements that constitute the true glory and beauty of a nation. First is the absence of disease, ensuring a healthy population. Second is economic wealth, followed by agricultural and productive yield. Fourth is the general happiness and well-being of the citizens. Finally, 'ēmam' refers to robust security and defense. The poet describes these five elements as 'aṇi' (ornaments), indicating that they are the crowning achievements that make a country truly beautiful and respected.

ai.literal: A country they say is that which has wealth without seeking; not a country is that which gives wealth when sought.
ai.translation: They say a true country is one that yields wealth without requiring laborious search; a land that yields wealth only when sought is no country at all.
ai.modern: முயற்சி செய்து தேடாமலேயே வளம் தரும் நாடே சிறந்த நாடு என்று கூறுவர்; தேடி முயற்சி செய்தால் மட்டுமே வளம் தரும் நாடு ஒரு நாடாகாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the ideal country based on its natural abundance. A truly great nation is one where resources and wealth are naturally plentiful, requiring no painful struggle or desperate seeking by its citizens. Conversely, a land where people must toil excessively and search hard just to obtain basic wealth does not deserve to be called a true country. The word 'நாடா' (without seeking) highlights effortless prosperity, while 'நாட' (upon seeking) emphasizes the burden of forced labor to extract wealth.

ai.literal: Even when having attained completeness there, there is indeed no benefit for a country that lacks harmony with its ruler.
ai.translation: Even if a country has acquired all other forms of excellence, it is of no use if it lacks a ruler who governs in harmony with his people.
ai.modern: அனைத்துச் சிறப்புகளையும் பெற்றிருந்தாலும், நல்லாட்சி செய்யும் அரசன் இல்லாத நாடு எந்தப் பயனையும் தராது.
ai.explanation: This couplet concludes the chapter on the country by emphasizing that physical and economic resources are meaningless without proper governance. The phrase 'vēntu amaivu' refers to the fitness of the ruler and the harmony between the ruler and the subjects. Even if a land possesses natural wealth, security, and prosperity, these assets yield no real benefit if there is no capable leader to manage and protect them. Thus, a good ruler is the ultimate requirement that gives value to all other virtues of a nation.
